system_description.narrative_title: AI‑infrastructure race fuels market, industrial and geopolitical disruption
system_description.narrative_summary: Across the headlines a single dominant narrative emerges: an accelerating AI boom—anchored by compute providers (notably Nvidia), data‑center and server capacity, and large AI platforms—is remaking industries (robotics, robotaxis, legal and enterprise tools) while concentrating market power. As an open system it links flows of capital, chips, cloud capacity, talent, data, and regulation across borders; shocks (price hikes, breaches, export controls, talent moves) flow in and out and generate reinforcing and balancing feedbacks that amplify volatility. The net effect is intense investment and consolidation, competitive product and price wars, rising cyber and export‑control friction (esp. US–China–Taiwan), and cascading market and operational risks.
system_description.scope: Within the system boundary: compute infrastructure (chips, servers, data centers), AI models and platforms, robotics/autonomy deployments, major firms and investors (e.g., Nvidia, OpenAI, Waymo, Chinese robotmakers), cloud/hyperscalers, supply‑chain logistics (chip manufacturing, server smuggling), regulatory and security actors, and market signals (earnings, analyst reports, stock moves).
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic‑technological ecosystem (global capital markets, international trade and geopolitics, and transnational supply chains).
adjacent_subsystems: National security & cyber operations (US, China, Taiwan)
Labor markets & consumer adoption of automation/robotics
evidence_headlines: Nvidia is the beating heart of the AI boom and the stock market — which sets up a big test
Nvidia customers face over 15% server price hikes as memory costs soar - report
China eases limits on Nvidia H200 chips as AI race escalates
OpenAI and Anthropic in price war as Chinese AI rivals gain ground
Waymo doubles spending on lobbying in robotaxi battle with Uber
China-linked hackers hit Taiwan in unprecedented ‘autonomous’ AI cyber attack

variables.name: Compute capacity
variables.description: Total available AI training and inference compute (e.g., aggregate FLOPS and usable accelerators) accessible across the system.

variables.name: Advanced chip manufacturing capacity
variables.description: Global production capability for specialized AI chips and related silicon (measured as throughput or maximum wafer-equivalent output).

variables.name: AI server inventory
variables.description: Quantity of deployable servers, GPU/accelerator racks, and supporting hardware available for AI infrastructure deployment.

variables.name: AI capital flow
variables.description: Rate at which investment capital (equity, debt, M&A funding) is entering AI infrastructure, platforms, and related ventures.

variables.name: AI model capability
variables.description: Aggregate performance, scale, and capability level of deployed and under-development AI models across the ecosystem.

variables.name: Data availability
variables.description: Volume, diversity, and accessibility of labeled and unlabeled data usable for training and operating AI systems.

variables.name: AI talent supply
variables.description: Available pool of skilled personnel (researchers, engineers, operators) qualified to build and run advanced AI systems.

variables.name: Cloud capacity utilization
variables.description: Fraction of cloud and hyperscaler capacity currently consumed by AI workloads versus available headroom.

variables.name: Supply‑chain disruption risk
variables.description: Probability and intensity of interruptions in logistics and component flows that affect AI hardware and infrastructure availability.

variables.name: Export control tightness
variables.description: Restrictiveness and enforcement intensity of trade and export controls that constrain cross-border flows of AI hardware and tech.

variables.name: Cyber attack rate
variables.description: Frequency and intensity of cyber intrusions, data breaches, and adversarial operations targeting AI infrastructure and datasets.

variables.name: Regulatory scrutiny intensity
variables.description: Level and assertiveness of regulatory oversight, investigations, and compliance enforcement focused on AI products and markets.

variables.name: Market concentration
variables.description: Degree to which AI infrastructure, platforms, and key inputs are dominated by a small number of large providers.

variables.name: Server price change rate
variables.description: Rate of price change (upward or downward) for servers, accelerators, memory, and other critical AI hardware components.

variables.name: Public trust in AI
variables.description: Aggregate level of public and user confidence or distrust in AI systems and their real-world deployments.

variables.name: AI operational deployment rate
variables.description: Speed and volume at which AI models and autonomous systems are being put into production and real-world use cases.

catalysts.title: Nvidia earnings / market reaction
catalysts.description: Nvidia's upcoming earnings announcement and accompanying guidance likely to move AI investment sentiment and hardware pricing expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'What Nvidia says on Wednesday to address concerns...' and multiple stories calling Nvidia earnings a market test.

catalysts.title: Groq racks come online
catalysts.description: Nvidia's integration and deployment of Groq rack systems after its purchase will add usable accelerator capacity to data centers this year.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Nvidia says Groq racks will be online this year following $20 billion purchase.'

catalysts.title: Meta launches Hatch agent platform
catalysts.description: Meta plans to release its Hatch AI agent platform in the coming weeks, expanding enterprise agent deployments and developer options.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Meta to launch Hatch AI agent platform in coming weeks.'

catalysts.title: Frontier model price competition
catalysts.description: Ongoing price cuts and competition among major model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Chinese rivals) will reshape access economics for model usage.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'OpenAI cuts developer pricing for frontier GPT-5.6 Sol...' and 'OpenAI and Anthropic in price war...'.

catalysts.title: China eases H200 chip limits (flow increase)
catalysts.description: Beijing's relaxation of restrictions on Nvidia H200 chips will likely increase legal imports and broader access to advanced accelerators in China.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'China eases limits on Nvidia H200 chips as AI race escalates.'

catalysts.title: Taiwan smuggling indictments and prosecutions
catalysts.description: Ongoing prosecutions and enforcement actions over alleged illegal export of AI servers/chips to China will affect illicit flows and raise cross‑strait enforcement pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Taiwan Charges Nine in Connection With Smuggling of AI Servers to China' and 'Taiwan issues indictments...'.

catalysts.title: Server and memory price pressure
catalysts.description: Reported memory cost increases and supplier pricing actions are driving >15% server price hikes for customers, pressuring deployment economics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia customers face over 15% server price hikes...' and 'memory costs soar'.

catalysts.title: SpaceX Nvidia-powered AI satellites (2027)
catalysts.description: SpaceX plans to orbit Nvidia-powered AI satellites next year, creating a new distributed compute/data node topology for certain workloads.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'SpaceX plans to put Nvidia-powered AI satellites in orbit next year.'

catalysts.title: Nvidia investment in data-center power (Cloverleaf)
catalysts.description: Nvidia's talks/investment in Cloverleaf Infrastructure will accelerate data‑center power and capacity expansion where finalized.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia invests in data center developer Cloverleaf Infrastructure' and 'in talks to invest in Cloverleaf.'

catalysts.title: Nvidia-Perplexity investment talks
catalysts.description: Ongoing talks for Nvidia to invest in Perplexity at a large valuation could deepen vendor ties to a leading model/assistant provider.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Nvidia in talks to invest in Perplexity at $30B valuation.'

catalysts.title: Brazil AI supercomputer push
catalysts.description: Brazil's national push for AI supercomputing, split across Chinese and US suppliers, will add regional compute and drive procurement dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Brazil launches AI supercomputer push, splits projects between Chinese, US firms.'

catalysts.title: Waymo testing in Munich and Germany rollout
catalysts.description: Waymo will begin testing autonomous vehicles in Munich and plans commercial driverless rides in Germany in 2027, advancing AV deployments in Europe.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Waymo to begin testing autonomous vehicles in Munich' and 'Waymo to launch driverless rides in Germany in 2027.'
